title: In Situ Liquid-Cell TEM Observation of Multiphase Classical and Nonclassical Nucleation of Calcium Oxalate

nodes.label: Calcium oxalate is the main kidney-stone mineral, so its nucleation and its inhibition by citrate matter clinically
How CaOx nucleates at the nanoscale, and how citrate blocks it, has never been watched directly
Real-time graphene-liquid-cell TEM with MD should reveal the pathway that fixes the final CaOx polymorph
Image CaOx nucleation inside a graphene liquid cell by TEM at constant electron dose

edges.mode_basis: F5 caption and the F5/F3 linked text require both steps together: excess Ca must first overcome the citrate buffer for anything to precipitate, and the citrate-bound water then fixes the hydrate
same sentence pair: 'the inhibiting effect of citrate is overcome, which causes formation of COD' and 'the citrate draws more water into the forming CaOx nucleus'

edges.note: audit: the caption says XRD shows the formation of COD with citrate, but only one pattern is plotted, so the panel cannot show a citrate-driven change of polymorph
audit: the EELS confidence intervals overlap, so only the EDS pair resolves the O:Ca increase the caption calls consistent
audit: no SAED, XRD or lattice image of the rectangular product is shown; the COM label rests on 90 degree corners
audit: the paper itself says MD gives insight rather than a direct comparison, which bounds the hydration mechanism
the F3 linked text weighs z-only growth, particle rotation and dissolution-reformation, and settles on the third only after the citrate argument
a beam artifact would undo the non-classical reading; the paper answers it with the constant dose rate and the shared cell of Figures 1 and 2

notes: Three pathways share one spine: classical (F1) and non-classical (F2) without citrate, plus the citrate control arm (F3-F4), all meeting at n17. 46 nodes, above the 25-40 aim, because the paper carries three parallel pathways plus an ex situ validation arm (SEM, XRD, EDS, EELS). No full text: the packet has captions plus linked text only, so every sample identity (with/without citrate), the 0.1 M citrate level, the 50 nm and 500 nm scale-bar lengths and the ~20 nm F3 particle size are text-only facts and are listed in attrs.requires_unseen. F2 is tier C6_unresolved and offers no panels, so o3-o5 carry figs F2 with empty panel_ids. All 12 offered panels are cited. No crop carries OCR cue classes, so no technique-cue check applied.

changes: n17 split: the conclusion stated two claims (pathway sets polymorph; citrate buffers and then yields COD). n17 keeps the first, new n20 carries the second; n16 -> n17 became n16 -> n20 and n20 -> n17 supports was added, so the spine still ends in one conclusion.

o5 split: the label read two things off F2 (90 degree corners at 67-76 s; coalescence by 85 s) and fed two different claims. o5 keeps the shape reading (-> n10), new o16 carries the coalescence (-> n9).
n16 attrs.mode set to 'joint': it is the only node with two incoming causes edges (n13, n14) and no caption offers a choice between them.

Added k2 -> n13 premise_for: n13 is a spine MEC claim (basis=argued) that had neither OBS evidence nor a KNW premise; the Ca:citrate over Ca:oxalate binding fact is the premise its equilibrium argument rests on.
Kept: 18 spine nodes in one connected path, 4 audits (a1, a2, d1, d2), all fair. o2, o11, o13, o14 and d2 were each considered for a split and kept: their clauses are one reading of one panel.

Note (no edit): the citrate arm runs PRC -> PRP/behavior_class (n12) -> MEC -> STR (n15, n16), so PRP precedes STR on that branch. This is the paper's own order (the transient-nucleation behaviour is what the citrate mechanism explains, and the polymorph follows from the mechanism), so the branch was left as built.
